conditional_input: The unreviewed self-contained heavy-four/rank-four candidate SHA256 91e125d73523e7e540b19d3b21d66946c6728304fd88f4833c920fad9cca5fa8. A rank-four heavy rectangle has two heavy lines on each side, each with two disjoint support-2 boundary rays partitioning the same four axes D.
finding: In this residual, the four heavy lines' support-pair partitions must, candidate-conditionally, consist of two distinct perfect matchings on D, each used twice. The two row lines must use the same matching and the two column lines the other. Thus the checkerboard assignment with one row and one column of each matching is candidate-excluded.
parity_proof: For any axis a in D, every heavy line has exactly one support-2 boundary cell using a. Join support-2 cells using a along their same-support pairings on low-only lines. Other rays on low-only lines may occur on a disjoint pair but cannot interfere with these pairings. The four high-line endpoints form two paths plus cycles, and the support pair is constant on each path; therefore every partner b in {a,b} occurs an even number of times among the four endpoints. The three perfect matchings of four axes give three distinct partners for a, so each matching occurs an even number of times among the four heavy lines: either one matching four times or two distinct matchings twice each. The first case is excluded by the same actual axis-group argument as in frontier-20261028-checkpoint-heavy4-support-graph-v1.json, without assuming that other support pairs never occur elsewhere: four boundary U rays align through the full-support core, and any additional a-axis support/basis cycle group would need at least five rows while the principal two-path group needs at least four, exceeding seven.
checkerboard_proof: Suppose high row 1 and high column 1 use matching P, while high row 2 and high column 2 use different matching Q. Fix a in D. Let U be the pair containing a in P and V the pair containing a in Q, so U and V meet only in a. The two U-boundary Q rays, at high row 1 and high column 1, are collinear with x because the shared full-support core ray is orthogonal to both and has nonzero U projection. Likewise the two V-boundary rays are collinear with y. The U and V boundary paths therefore each have same-ray endpoints, odd size, one high-row and one high-column endpoint, and at least two incident rows. Group all support-2 cells using a by pair and 2D basis. Distinct groups have nonzero Q cross-overlap and mutually orthogonal mate spans; 8−K outside rows supply light Q=e_a mate rays. Exact dimension saturation gives each group its row count. Any additional cycle-only group needs at least five rows by three disjoint transition supports, but the two principal path groups already use at least four and K<=7, so none exists. In each principal group, the endpoint-ray mate class is an ONB and the perpendicular-ray class has one fewer ray; let E_U and E_V be the one-dimensional residuals. The two off-diagonal heavy Q rays are perpendicular to x and y and therefore lie in span{x,y}-perpendicular. If independent, their common orthogonal space is span{x,y}, which uses only the three axes of U union V; the diagonal heavy ray, orthogonal to both, could not have full support D. Hence the off-diagonal heavy Q rays are collinear p. For every mate their two rays are orthogonal and lie in E_U plus E_V, hence form its ONB. Each diagonal mate ray is orthogonal to both p mate rays by shared row/column. Its full-support Q ray is perpendicular to its own boundary ray, so it overlaps the perpendicular-ray class of its own group; it therefore has no component in that group's non-residual subspace. If the first diagonal Q ray overlapped the opposite boundary y, its mate ray would also be orthogonal to the y-class ONB, forcing it to zero. Thus it is perpendicular to y; similarly the other diagonal Q ray is perpendicular to x. The diagonal Q rays are both perpendicular to x,y,p and are therefore collinear. They overlap the perpendicular-ray classes of both groups, so their mate rays lie in E_U plus E_V while being orthogonal to its p-ray ONB, contradiction.
exact_remaining_gap: The remaining matching arrangement has both heavy rows using P and both heavy columns using different Q. Its axis-a boundary paths connect two high rows for the P-pair and two high columns for the Q-pair, giving even paths and unequal group row/column counts. The previous odd-path exact-saturation argument cannot be transferred unchanged. Other heavy counts and the global four-family problem remain open.
